title: Rigveda 10.149: To Savitri
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.149: To Savitri: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.149 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Savitri. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 133v-134r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.149.1 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 133v
translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>sa̱vi̱tā ya̱ntraiḥ pṛ̍thi̱vīm a̍ramṇād askambha̱ne sa̍vi̱tā dyām a̍dṛṁhat | aśva̍m ivādhukṣa̱d dhuni̍m a̱ntari̍kṣam a̱tūrte̍ ba̱ddhaṁ sa̍vi̱tā sa̍mu̱dram ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>SAVITAR fixed the earth with bands to bind it, and made heaven stedfast where no prop supported. Savitar milked, as 'twere a restless courser, air, sea bound fast to what no foot had trodden.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 133v (OPenn image 133, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.148.3 ‹-enota tubhyaṁ rathoḻha bhakṣaiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 134r, begins in RV 10.149.2 ‹dyāvāpṛthivī aprathetām›. Verse 10.149.1 ends on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.149.2-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 134r
translation.original_text:
2yatrā̍ samu̱draḥ ska̍bhi̱to vy auna̱d apā̍ṁ napāt savi̱tā tasya̍ veda | ato̱ bhūr ata̍ ā̱ utthi̍ta̱ṁ rajo 'to̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī a̍prathetām ||
3pa̱ścedam a̱nyad a̍bhava̱d yaja̍tra̱m ama̍rtyasya̱ bhuva̍nasya bhū̱nā | su̱pa̱rṇo a̱ṅga sa̍vi̱tur ga̱rutmā̱n pūrvo̍ jā̱taḥ sa u̍ a̱syānu̱ dharma̍ ||
4gāva̍ iva̱ grāma̱ṁ yūyu̍dhir i̱vāśvā̍n vā̱śreva̍ va̱tsaṁ su̱manā̱ duhā̍nā | pati̍r iva jā̱yām a̱bhi no̱ ny e̍tu dha̱rtā di̱vaḥ sa̍vi̱tā vi̱śvavā̍raḥ ||
5hira̍ṇyastūpaḥ savita̱r yathā̍ tvāṅgira̱so ju̱hve vāje̍ a̱smin | e̱vā tvārca̱nn ava̍se̱ vanda̍māna̱ḥ soma̍syevā̱ṁśum prati̍ jāgarā̱ham ||
translation.text:
2Well knoweth Savitar, O Child of Waters, where ocean, firmly fixt, o'erflowed its limit. Thence sprang the world, from that uprose the region: thence heaven spread out and the wide earth expanded.
3Then, with a full crowd of Immortal Beings, this other realm came later, high and holy. First, verily, Savitar's strong-pinioned Eagle was born: and he obeys his law for ever.
4As warriors to their steeds, kine to their village, as fond milk giving cows approach their youngling, As man to wife, let Savitar come downward to us, heaven's bearer, Lord of every blessing.
5Like the Ângirasa Hiraṇyastûpa, I call thee, Savitar, to this achievement: So worshipping and lauding thee for favour I watch for thee as for the stalk of Soma.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 134r (OPenn image 133, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.149.2 ‹dyāvāpṛthivī aprathetām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 134v, begins in RV 10.150.1 ‹-mṛḻīkāya na ā gahi›. Verses 10.149.2-5 end on this page; 10.149.2 begins on fol. 133v.
